body.statement: The law \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\) in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) for the displayed admissible constants and is nondegenerate: its responses have bounded nonzero conditional noise, its design point is interior, and its full stacked donor covariance is positive definite with nonzero off-diagonal entries. Let \(\bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd}\). For every \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), set \(u_\delta=\delta\Sigma\bar e/(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\). Then \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2=\delta\) and \(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta=\delta(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}>0\). Consequently, when \(\kappa=1\), the weighted surface has nonzero standardized gradient and its increment along \(u_\delta\) is \(\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\delta/64+O(\delta^2)\); when \(0<\kappa<1\), the positive asymmetric-cusp increment is \(\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{\kappa/2}\delta^{\kappa}/64\). Hence \(\omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^{\kappa}\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\). This construction establishes non-vacuity only and does not derive the lower modulus for the general panel class.
body.proof_tex:
Set
\[
 a_0=\frac{\min\{B,L,1\}}{64},\qquad
 \bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd},
 \qquad q_0=(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}.
\]
Because \(B>0\) and \(L>0\), we have \(a_0>0\).  We first verify,
condition by condition, that the law constructed in
\texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} is a member of the class in
\texttt{def:panel-model-class}.

For the donor law, \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} gives
\[
 \Sigma=\frac12 I_{Sd}
       +\frac{1}{2Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}^{\top}.
\]
The eigenvalue in the direction \(\mathbf 1_{Sd}\) is one, while the
eigenvalue on its orthogonal complement is one half.  Thus \(\Sigma\) is
positive definite, \(q_0>0\), and the displayed restrictions
\(c_\Sigma\le 1/2\) and \(C_\Sigma\ge 1\) imply
\[
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}.
\]
This proves \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Every off-diagonal entry that
exists equals \(1/(2Sd)>0\); in particular, when \(Sd\ge2\), the covariance
has nonzero cross-coordinate or cross-cohort entries.

The vectors \((U_j)_{j=1}^{N}\) are independent and identically distributed,
\(\mathbb E[U_j]=0\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(U_j)=I_{Sd}\).  Since the
square root in the construction is the symmetric positive square root,
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)
 =\Sigma^{1/2}I_{Sd}\Sigma^{1/2}=\Sigma.
\]
Hence \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and
\texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness} hold.  Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[
   \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\mid z_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E[\|U_j\|_2^4]
 =(Sd)^2\le B^4,
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.

We next check the outcome and causal restrictions.  Both displayed formulas
for \(m_1\) give \(m_1(z_{01})=4a_0\), and
\(m_s(z_{0s})=4a_0\) for \(s>1\).  Therefore
\[
 B_{si}(0)\in\{3a_0,5a_0\},
 \qquad
 B_{si}(1)\in\{4a_0,6a_0\}.
\]
In particular \(B_{si}(a)>0\), so
\(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), as required by the support of a simple
return.  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level}, \(W_{si,-1}=1\), and
\(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\),
\[
 W_{si,-1}\prod_{h=0}^{H}\{1+R_{sih}(a)\}
 =1\cdot B_{si}(a)\prod_{h=1}^{H}1
 =B_{si}(a),
\]
where the last product is empty and equals one when \(H=0\).  The prescribed
identity \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) is
\texttt{ass:consistency}.  Centering of \(\eta_{si}\), together with its
independence from \(z_0\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0\mathbb E[\eta_{si}\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s}),
\]
which is \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}.

For boundedness, first suppose \(\kappa=1\) and write
\(y=x_1-1/2\).  Since \(y\in[-1/2,1/2]\),
\[
 -\frac14\le y+y^2\le\frac34,
 \qquad
 \frac{15a_0}{4}\le m_1(x)\le\frac{19a_0}{4}.
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), the two one-sided terms cannot be nonzero
simultaneously, and consequently
\[
 \frac{7a_0}{2}\le m_1(x)\le5a_0.
\]
Every other surface equals \(4a_0\).  Since both noise arrays take values in
\(\{-1,1\}\), these bounds imply
\[
 |Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|
 \le6a_0
 \le\frac{6B}{64}<B.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds.  The response noise is nonzero because,
with \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T})\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(B_{si}(a)\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0.
\]

We now verify \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  If \(0<\lambda<1\), then
\(\kappa=\lambda\).  For \(a,b\ge0\), differentiation of
\(\phi(t)=(1+t)^\lambda-1-t^\lambda\) gives
\(\phi'(t)=\lambda\{(1+t)^{\lambda-1}-t^{\lambda-1}\}\le0\) for
\(t>0\), while \(\phi(0)=0\).  After rescaling, this proves
\((a+b)^\lambda\le a^\lambda+b^\lambda\).  Applying this inequality to
the larger and smaller of \(v_+\) and \(w_+\), and using that the positive-part
map is one-Lipschitz, yields
\[
 |v_+^\lambda-w_+^\lambda|\le |v-w|^\lambda,
 \qquad
 |(-v)_+^\lambda-(-w)_+^\lambda|\le |v-w|^\lambda.
\]
When \(v\) and \(w\) have opposite signs, each of \(|v|\) and \(|w|\)
is at most \(|v-w|\), so the asymmetric cusp has H\"older constant at most
\(3/2\).  As \(|x_1-x'_1|\le\|x-x'\|_2\),
\[
 \|m_1\|_\infty+[m_1]_\lambda
 \le5a_0+\frac32a_0
 =\frac{13}{2}a_0<L.
\]
If \(\lambda\ge1\), the selected surface is quadratic, and its only nonzero
derivatives of positive order are
\[
 \partial_1m_1(x)=a_0\{1+2(x_1-1/2)\},
 \qquad
 \partial_{11}m_1(x)=2a_0.
\]
The first derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\) and is Lipschitz with constant
\(2a_0\); the second derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\); and every derivative
of order greater than two vanishes.  For \(1<\lambda<2\), Lipschitzness and
\(|x_1-x'_1|\le1\) imply the required \((\lambda-1)\)-H\"older bound on the
first derivative.  For \(\lambda>2\), the highest derivative required by the
H\"older norm is constant or zero.  At integer \(\lambda\), the stated
order-reduction convention gives the same bounds.  Thus the standard
isotropic H\"older norm is at most
\[
 \frac{19}{4}a_0+2a_0+2a_0<9a_0<L.
\]
The constant surfaces have norm \(4a_0<L\).  Hence every \(m_s\) belongs to
\(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\).  The first surface is non-affine: it has a
nonzero quadratic term when \(\kappa=1\) and an asymmetric cusp when
\(0<\kappa<1\).

The \(X_{st}\) are independent and uniform on \([0,1]^d\), so their common
density is \(f_X(x)=1\).  Because \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), this is
\texttt{ass:design-density}.  Furthermore,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:interior-path}.  Independence across calendar
windows makes the joint calendar sequence independent, and hence
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\qquad(k\ge1).
\]
This is \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.

Conditional on \((z_0,\mathcal X)\), centering and independence of the noises
give
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
These are exactly the two equalities in
\texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  Conditional on
\((z_0,\mathcal X)\), each unit history is generated by that unit's own
\((\varepsilon_{sti})_{t=1}^{T}\) and \(\eta_{si}\).  Their mutual
independence across \((s,i)\) proves
\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  The construction records each
\(X_{st}\) directly, which is \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.

Finally, define
\[
 \mathcal Z=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}),
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{panel}}
 =\sigma((X_{st},Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i}).
\]
Under the product-law construction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp},
\(\mathcal Z\) is generated by the donor Rademacher array, whereas
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{panel}}\) is generated by the independent design,
training-noise, and event-noise arrays.  Therefore, for every
\(A\in\mathcal Z\) and \(C\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{panel}}\),
\[
 \mathbb P(A\cap C\mid z_0)
 =\mathbb P(A\mid z_0)\mathbb P(C\mid z_0).
\]
This is the full donor-versus-joint-panel factorization required by the
clarified \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}.  All member conditions of
\texttt{def:panel-model-class} have now been verified, and hence
\[
 P_{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}.
\]

It remains to prove the asserted local-modulus order from
\texttt{def:local-modulus}.  For \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), set
\[
 u_\delta=\frac{\delta\Sigma\bar e}{q_0}.
\]
Since \(q_0^2=\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e\),
\[
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2^2
 =\frac{\delta^2}{q_0^2}\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e
 =\delta^2,
 \qquad
 \bar e^{\top}u_\delta=\delta q_0>0.
\]
The radius restriction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} also yields
\[
 \|u_\delta\|_\infty
 \le\delta_0\|\Sigma\bar e/q_0\|_\infty
 \le\frac12.
\]
Because \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), it follows that
\(z_0+u_\delta\in([0,1]^d)^S\).  Thus \(u_\delta\) is feasible in the
supremum defining \(\omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\).

If \(\kappa=1\), the stacked gradient of the weighted surface at \(z_0\) is
\(\pi_1a_0\bar e\), whose covariance-standardized dual norm is
\[
 \|\Sigma^{1/2}(\pi_1a_0\bar e)\|_2
 =\pi_1a_0q_0>0.
\]
Writing \(u_{\delta,s}\) for the cohort-\(s\) block of \(u_\delta\), direct
substitution gives
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0(q_0\delta+q_0^2\delta^2)
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0}{64}\delta+O(\delta^2).
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), positivity of
\(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta\) selects the positive cusp branch, and
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0q_0^\kappa\delta^\kappa
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0^\kappa}{64}\delta^\kappa.
\]
Since \(a_0>0\), \(q_0>0\), and \(\pi_1>0\), these displays give a constant
\(c_{\mathrm{ex}}>0\), depending only on the fixed displayed parameters,
such that
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)
 \ge c_{\mathrm{ex}}\delta^\kappa
 \qquad(0<\delta\le\delta_0).
\]

For the reverse inequality, let \(u\) be any feasible perturbation in
\texttt{def:local-modulus}.  By the upper ellipticity bound,
\[
 \|u\|_2
 =\|\Sigma^{1/2}\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
Put \(v=\bar e^{\top}u\).  Feasibility of \(z_0+u\) gives
\(|v|\le1/2\), and also \(|v|\le\|u\|_2\).  When \(\kappa=1\),
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 =a_0|v+v^2|
 \le\frac32a_0|v|
 \le\frac32a_0C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
When \(0<\kappa<1\), either branch of the asymmetric cusp gives
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 \le a_0|v|^\kappa
 \le a_0C_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\delta^\kappa.
\]
All other cohort surfaces are constant and \(0<\pi_1\le1\).  Taking the
supremum over feasible \(u\), we obtain a finite constant
\(C_{\mathrm{ex}}>0\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)
 \le C_{\mathrm{ex}}\delta^\kappa
 \qquad(0<\delta\le\delta_0).
\]
Combining the last two bounds proves
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^\kappa
 \qquad\text{as }\delta\downarrow0.
\]
The lower bound was derived only for this explicit law; it was not imposed as
a condition on every member of the base H\"older class.
body.justification: The explicit calculation exhibits a bounded noisy member of the base Holder panel class with a non-affine response surface and a sharp local modulus, without imposing a class-wide lower-modulus condition.
body.gap: The headline global frontier uses explicit worst-case witnesses and assumes no attainable direction for every law; this proposition separately records a concrete sensitive nondegenerate member rather than claiming that Holder smoothness alone implies attainability.
body.consumer: Referees can audit a legal bounded DGP with a sharp local modulus independently of the explicit witness families used for the headline donor converse.
